thread.title: Intraday Update: Treads Water as Market Waits…and Waits…and Waits

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Treads Water as Market Waits…and Waits…and Waits
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 8, 2018 1:21 p.m. ET Buy on the rumor, sell on the news.
So goes the trader’s shanty, and Tuesday morning they were so ahead of themselves when it came to the oil market that they weren’t even selling on the news, they were selling on leaked rumors of the news .
Illustration: Getty Images The betting is that President Donald Trump will announce at 2:00 p.m. that the U.S. is pulling out of the Iran nuclear deal. What this will mean and where this will lead has yet to be seen. But Iran is the fourth-biggest producer of oil, with 5% of world production, and has the third-largest reserves, at just under 10%.
Sanctions ought to be bullish for oil, but the crude price settled back nearly 3%, falling below $69 by lunchtime. The likely explanation: Traders who had been betting on oil, and making out like bandits as the price spiked over recent weeks, decided to take some profits ahead of this afternoon.
Well, you would, wouldn’t you?
Among U.S. oil majors, benchmark Exxon Mobil (XOM), which was recently featured in a Barron's cover story , was off 0.7% by lunchtime, while Chevron (CVX) was slightly in the black. Who benefits from rising oil prices? The U.S. recently edged out Saudi Arabia as the world’s top producer. No. 3: Russia.
Meanwhile, the major stock indexes were seeking direction, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average easing 80 points and the Standard & Poor’s 500 a third of a percent. The U.S. Dollar Index continued its recent Kudlow boomlet. One euro now buys less than $1.19.
Treasury yields are on the march again following further news that the job market continues to boom. Job openings are up to 6.6 million. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 0.03 points to 2.98%.
Apple (AAPL) is holding on to its new highs, edging up slightly to stay above $185.
Goldman Sachs Group (GS) edged up a dollar following a Bloomberg report that the conspiracy theorists’ favorite investment bank is thinking about launching its own credit card . The loyalty program alone could be to die for. How many points do you need to join the Illuminati?
Midday Movers AES (AES) is down 3% to $12 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The utility earned 28 cents a share on revenue of $2.74 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 25 cents a share on revenue of $3.13 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn between $1.15 and $1.25 a share, compared with the $1.19 per-share consensus estimate.
Expeditors International of Washington (EXPD) is up 8.1% to $69.16 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The logistics company earned 76 cents a share on revenue of $1.85 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 65 cents on revenue of $1.72 billion.
Gartner (IT) is up 5% to $130.03 on first-quarter earnings . The research and advisory company earned 72 cents a share on revenue of $964 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of 58 cents on revenue of $921.22 million. for the full year it expects to earn between $3.51 and $3.91 a share on revenue of $3.93 billion to $4.94 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $3.86 a share on revenue of $4.11 billion consensus.
Jacobs Engineering Group (JEC) is up 7.6% to $61.11 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The engineering firm earned $1 a share on revenue of $3.94 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 87 cents a share on revenue of $3.6 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn between $4 and $4.40 a share, above its previous guidance of $3.85 to $4.25 a share and the $3.94 per-share consensus estimate.
Martin Marietta Materials (MLM) is up 3.7% to $212.12 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The construction-materials firm earned 16 cents a share on revenue of $802 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 23 cents on revenue of $822.23 million. For the full year, it raised its guidance, saying it now expects revenue between $4.3 billion and $4.5 billion, above the $4.27 billion consensus. — Teresa Rivas
Keeping an Eye on...Caterpillar Caterpillar 's stock (CAT) got pounded on April 24 after the company used the term "high-water mark" to describe its earnings. At a Wells Fargo conference, it tried to walk that comment back .
Independent analyst Al Root notes that management said the direction of revenue is positive, and that it was only the pace of estimate revisions that had peaked—not the earnings themselves. "The question going forward is 2019 earnings peak?" Root writes. "If not then margin fears generated by higher commodity prices will end up being an opportunity. This debate will likely run thru the summer."
Investors don't appear to be taking sides today, as shares of Caterpillar gained 0.2% to $160.01 at 11:52 a.m.
But it could be a long summer. — Ben Levisohn
